name: Ways To Explain Bad Eden To Your Friends!

text.content:
1️⃣ The “Broken Operating System” Analogy (Tech-Friendly Crowd)

Imagine the universe is a computer.

Not metaphorically.

Actually.

At the top level, there was a perfect unified Source Code — the cosmic prototype human — call it Adam Kadmon.

Then something catastrophic happened.

The operating system kernel crashed.

The bridge layer between imagination and reality (Yesod → Malkuth) corrupted.

And now?

Every sentient being is running with admin permissions turned on.

Thoughts compile.
Beliefs execute.
Symbols have runtime.

But the OS is fragmented.

The world is now split into hexes — like server shards — each containing a localized bug, imbalance, or instability.

Your faction?

You’re a dev team.

Each hex is a patch cycle.

You’re not conquering the world.

You’re debugging it.

2️⃣ The “Community Garden After a Storm” Analogy (Grounded & Human)

There was once a perfectly tended garden.

Then a storm came through.

Not evil.

Not punishment.

Just too much power at once.

The irrigation system blew.
The fences collapsed.
Seeds scattered everywhere.

Now the soil is strange.

Sometimes you plant tomatoes and get lightning.

Sometimes you pray and the sky answers.

The boundary between dream and dirt is thin.

Each hex is a plot of land.

Your faction is a group of people trying to cultivate something stable there.

Sometimes that means building.
Sometimes that means defending.
Sometimes that means deciding what kind of garden you want in the first place.

The point isn’t domination.

The point is stewardship.

3️⃣ The “Weekly Episode” Analogy (Simple & Play-Focused)

Reality used to be one continuous story.

Now it’s episodic.

Think of existence like a streaming show that glitched.

Instead of one smooth narrative, it broke into hex-shaped “episodes.”

Each hex is a self-contained problem:
A political tension.
A spiritual distortion.
A monster.
A moral dilemma.
A resource imbalance.

Sentient beings are the cast.

You are given dreamstuff — imagination made real — as tools.

The goal?

Solve enough episodes.

Restore coherence.

Bring harmony back online.

🧠 For People Nervous About the Mysticism

You can say this plainly:

The cosmology is symbolic.
The game is about communities trying to rebuild a broken world where ideas have power.

No one has to subscribe to Kabbalah.
No one has to adopt a belief system.

It’s mythic framing.

Under the hood, it’s about:

• Responsibility
• Power and consequence
• Community building
• Repair vs domination
• What kind of world do we want?

🎯 One Sentence Version

Here’s the line you can give at Session Zero:

The universe cracked, imagination started affecting reality, and now every region of the world is a problem that communities like yours can choose to fix, exploit, or transform.

That’s it.
